chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Joe Garland and In the Mood
summary: He says Joe Garland wrote In the Mood and Leapfrog and made Glenn Miller popular, though the public credits Miller.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: He wasn't involved in other things - I remember now, Leeds used to put out band arrangements. Like 'String of Pearls' and stuff like that by Glenn Miller and so forth. Did Glenn Miller get his stuff from Fletcher Henderson? A lot of people said that Glenn Miller was just a bigger orchestration of Fletcher Henderson.
The only thing that made Glenn Miller popular is Joe Garland when he wrote 'In the Mood.'
Yeah, that made him the most popular band.

I don't know. I was in Lucky Millinder's band then. He wrote 'In the Mood' and he wrote 'Leapfrog', Joe Garland did. He wrote 'Leapfrog' after he wrote In the Mood, but 'In the Mood' made him rich and today you can't make nobody believe that Glenn Miller didn't write 'In the Mood.' Glenn Miller didn't have nothing to do with it.
How did he get it from Joe? If he just copied and made an arrangement of it. But he said that he wrote the tune? Glenn Miller claims that he wrote the tune?
Glenn didn't. I mean that's what the public thinks.
